We don't offer facts. We offer vibes.
We don't offer science. We offer swagger.
And we definitely don't offer anything you should actually follow.

Come for the satire, stay for the spectacle, hope you don't leave with a ne

places.name: Tower of Ascension
places.desc: The human ape, grounded and evolving from a single cell blob in a sea of primordial mud, pushes up towards the light, climbing the ladder of an elongated spine, reaching for the stars, beholds the glory and terror of its own existence, begins to comprehend its connection to everything, slowly realizing itself as nothing less than the entirety of existence, the eternal "I AM" looking through its ow

places.name: Sapta Dvāra (The 7th Gate)
places.desc: Sapta Dvāra (The 7th Gate) explores the intersection of light, passage, and transformation. Inspired by the mythic act of walking through light to awaken inner truth, the installation symbolizes courage, renewal, and impermanence. A sequence of aligned gates forms a luminous corridor that shifts from quiet presence by day to radiant color by night. Motion-triggered light flows through the structur

places.name: Now + Next
places.desc: Now + Next is a crossroads of contemplation.  A fanciful mosaic street sign at the corner of "Be Here Now" and What's Next?" Grounded in earth, granite, wood, flowers and reaching for the sky.

places.name: Windoors Vista
places.desc: Tiny worlds are hidden behind doors within doors. Like accidentally clicking a pop-up ad, behind every door lies a carefully curated surprise, though thankfully none of them will ask you to update Adobe Flash Player.

places.name: Cellubrate
places.desc: Cellubrate reminds you that you used to be a sperm. The spermatozoon is an unmistakable symbol of fertility, but also a reminder of our origins. Nearly every nonbacterial species has a flagellated gamete phase – including you! This wooden monument celebrates the grand trajectory of life, where all our ancestry unites back to a single universal cell. A single sperm embarks on a futile quest; only w

places.name: Time Drop
places.artist: Jordan MacHardy, Sonia Aggarwal, Scott MacHardy, Wes MacHardy, Kasey Boekholt
places.desc: Time Drop gives you the ability to control the rate and direction of time in an infinite rain storm...and uses time travel to help people solve minor plumbing issues.

places.name: The Black Rock Guidestones
places.desc:
The Black Rock Guidestones rise in defiance of the arsonists who destroyed the mysterious Georgia Guidestones - a formation meant to offer humanity guidance in the event of a global cataclysm.

A 1:1 scale adaptation of that intent, suited to our culture and moment, re-imagined in the desert. Three 20-foot, double-sided panels invite us to remember our responsibility to one another and the large

places.name: STOP and Reflect
places.desc:
STOP and Reflect is a giant traffic signal in deep playa.  It is best viewed at night when it is brightly lit against the inky black darkness of the playa.  

Burning Man can be a frenzied experience...When the light is RED Burners are encouraged to STOP wherever they are, appreciate the art that surrounds them, take a moment to soak in the experience, form a lifetime memory, and move on again whe

places.name: The Starting Line
places.desc: The Starting Line presents a familiar race structure reimagined as a moment of beginning. It represents the shift from reflection to action, what is released during the burn and what is carried forward after it ends. Rooted in the idea of taking the first mile toward who one wants to become, the piece honors the spirit of a fellow Burner and the belief that meaningful change starts with a single s

places.name: Build Better Ruins
places.desc: "Build Better Ruins" is a phrase from the 'doomster' author Dougald Hine. Paraphrasing his work: If we find we are living in a time of endings, and the narratives of modernity no longer speak to our future realities, how then would we want to re-imagine our world? What would "better" ruins look like? This bio-punk sculpture, using common street infrastructure widgets, is my effort to answer Hines'

places.name: Spin Your ASS!--Fun With Angular Momentum!
places.hometown: Ames, Iowa & New York, New York
places.desc: Experience speed without distance through revolutionary angular momentum.  At the center of the merry-go-round, stand straight and tall and feel your shifting weight translate into revolutionary motion. Become the axis and have a look around!  Eyes on the horizon, and remember to BREATHE!

places.name: Giraffe in Motion
places.desc: Giraffe in Motion is a life-size LED push puppet that comes to life (powered by YOU)!

places.name: REAL LOVE
places.desc: REAL LOVE is a multimedia project for Burning Man 2026 by acclaimed Ukrainian artist Alexander Milov. The project brings together a monumental sculpture — the final work in a series that began with Milov’s iconic LOVE, unveiled at Burning Man in 2015 — a traveling exhibition of miniature sculptures from the same body of work, and a participatory documentary film woven from visitors’ stories, explo

places.name: Teeny Weeny Hooter Tooter
places.desc: Teeny Weeny Hooter Tooter is a set of 4 small teeters that Burners can ride up and down on to create music.  The teeters operate leather bellows that supply air to 8 sets of handmade wooden organ pipes.  The walls supporting the pipes are adorned with additional random instruments and art to be played with and enjoyed.

places.name: ancient future portal
places.desc:
A 20 foot tall hand carved wooden sculpture composed of a central form supported by four angled legs. Its shape suggests an artifact that feels both ancient and unfamiliar, as if from a culture that has encountered something beyond its understanding.

A circular opening sits within the form, covered by a subtle film that suggests a veil between the visible world and something less defined. The s

places.name: Illumicone
places.desc:
Illumicone is light art driven by participation and interaction. A softly glowing presence draws participants inside, where they encounter strange mechanical widgets. As they play with the widgets, patterns of light move in response, surrounding the participants with a dazzling spectacle of color of their own creation.

Illumicone is 19 feet tall at its center and 38 feet across at its base. Cab

places.name: VORTEX
places.desc: VORTEX is a trio of illuminated cubes set against the open desert, scaled at 2m, 3m, and 4m. Each form is wrapped in a continuous black-and-white spiral printed onto tensioned Lycra, creating the illusion of a deep, collapsing void. By day, the stark geometry fractures perception against the horizon; by night, the cubes glow from within, transforming into luminous beacons. The work explores percep

places.name: Ethereal Essence of Odin
places.desc: The beauty of this magnificent creature and the indisputable, genuine love, loyalty and friendship for all beings. By placing him on the playa facing the Man, we hope to convey the inner feeling of humanity, the bond between a human and a dog and the connection we all share.

places.name: Shroomie-Go-Round
places.desc: This combines thrill and community within deep playa. The swinging structure has four seats, and can whirl you around in a circle. It's the perfect place to admire the stars and bask in the desert beauty.

places.name: A Pretty Cool S
places.desc:
It's the S we all know how to draw. Did someone show us how to draw it, or did we all just figure it out?

Wikipedia says Stussy denies creating it, and it has nothing to do with Superman.

places.name: Voxelite
places.desc: Voxelite transforms three-dimensional space into a canvas of light, responding to interaction with rippling patterns that seem to communicate in a visual language all its own. No two encounters are identical, as this photon playground dialogues with those who discover it—every visit revealing a different pattern within its luminous architecture. Venture into a realm where light doesn't just shine—

places.name: Reactor Wing
places.desc: The Reactor Project brings this futuristic pyramid altar. Play, hide, swing, react and interact with its beautiful geometry.

places.name: Fractured Light
places.artist: Andrew Ratliff, Emily Ratliff, Griffin Ratliff
places.desc: Fractured Light is an attempt at balance. There are two circles of pillars. The outer circle has eight points, like the eight pointed star revered in most cultures throughout history. Each pillar has designs cut into it so colorful light can come out and create fantastic designs all around. In the center stands a white pillar, representing the culmination of all the shapes and colors, coming toget

places.name: Bar That Never Opened
places.hometown: Chicago, IL; Chelyabinsk, Russia & Moscow, Russia
places.desc:
An interactive installation built as a fragment of a bar interior — a small space where visitors can occasionally drink coffee or tea, watch television, or listen to vinyl records.

The work explores unfinished stories and human presence, where meaning emerges through shared experience rather than consumption. With only two seats, the installation emphasizes intimate encounters between strangers

places.name: Tenseract
places.desc: tensegrity + tesseract = tenseract

places.name: Another Mother
places.desc: Tabitha the Tarantula Hawk has received an invitation to A Svengali Gala taking place way out by The Trash Fence. She must now quickly subdue her latest conquest while she contemplates what to wear to this most hypnotic occasion.

places.name: Reflection Connection
places.desc: Reflection Connection is, in simple terms, a disco ball phone booth. It invites participants to both reflect and connect with themselves and others through its fragmented mirrors and light refractions. It evokes whimsy, turning the concept of a utilitarian phone booth on its head, to spark curiosity and wonder. It represents the light and sparkle in all of us.

places.name: Atlas Endures
places.desc: Atlas Endures depicts the Titan condemned by Zeus to bear the heavens for eternity as punishment for siding with the Titans against the Olympian gods. Crouched atop a pedestal, arms spread wide to support the celestial sphere above him. Atlas endures the blazing sun from rise to set; then, under a darkened sky, he holds the moon, the Pleiades, and Orion, marking the eternal passage between day and

places.name: windswept
places.desc: Standing a commanding nine feet tall, this sculpture "windswept" makes the viewer look up. Made from industrial steel, the rigidity and durability mirrors the tempered strength of the feminine spirit. Her eyes are peacefully closed not in a sign of surrender, but of profound internal focus - the ability to find a centered "inner calm" while navigating external headwinds.

places.name: The Lust Stop
places.desc: The Lust Stop is the playa mutant bus stop. From its location in the deep playa, it offers BRC citizens an opportunity to board rides that might stop by and pick them up. We provide a route map of different bus/mutant vehicle services that might be in service with tentative schedules. As citizens wait for the ride, they can enjoy the comfort of a fur-covered bench and have shade over their heads a

places.name: Stellar
places.desc:
Stellar is an artwork representing nebula.
Through Stellar, we want to remind ourselves of the vastness of our world and how, on a scale this large, we, humanity, are a single unity rather than divided by differences.

(We don't want to minimize anyone or anything, but we do want to emphasize the wider connection we all share.)

places.name: Well, Well, Well
places.artist: Youtian Duan, Kai Zhang, Chuwei Zheng, Trapper Alswo,  Forrest Carper
places.hometown: Eugene, OR; Seattle, WA;  Los Angeles, CA; Brooklyn, NY
places.desc: Well, Well, Well is a full-scale wishing well standing in the deep playa. In a place with no water, it is the last thing anyone expects to find and the first thing everyone recognizes. A windlass frame straddles the rim, a rope hangs into the dark, and at the bottom sits a screen showing quietly moving water. When the crank is turned, a bucket descends and a short phrase surfaces, something betwee

places.name: The Speed of the Earth 2026
places.desc: The Speed of the Earth art installation enables participants to sense the speed of the Earth by carefully coordinating a mile-long row of strobes to flash at the rate of Earth's rotation at the latitude of Black Rock City. The timed flash rushes along the line of strobes placed exactly east-to-west, just as the Earth rotates, at the exact speed of the rotation. Standing still, a participant sees t

places.name: Temple Braziers
places.desc: The Temple Brazier is a wooden altar at the entrance to the Temple of the Moon, and serves as focal point for the ancient spiritual practice of burning incense (palo santo, sage, and others) allowing deep connection and spiritual expression.

places.name: untitled (omphalos)
places.desc: Untitled (omphalos) is a sculptural installation composed of eleven burned firewood towers and two viewing platforms made from sanded, charred wood. Rising from the open playa, the work imagines the omphalos, the mythic center of the universe, as a place of threshold and convergence. The blackened towers form a gathering point between opposing forces: life and death, striving and surrender, doing

places.name: Playa Swirls
places.desc: Playa Swirl is a colorful sculpture made with 300 paper lanterns that have been coated with epoxy resin. They are suspended overhead and create a calming and relaxing place to enjoy the playa.  During the day the lanterns are lit by the sun and during the night each lantern will be illuminated by LEDs.

places.name: Surfwheel 2.0
places.desc: A large surfboard pinwheel, made from hand painted, repurposed boards from the playas of Southern California, to the playa of BRC, inspiring awe as it spins with the wind.

places.name: Solar Prisms
places.desc: Solar Prisms is a collection of cuboctahedrons comprised of solar panels and light diffusers. They capture light, store it as energy, and emit it again as a colorful and beautiful light show. They can be placed anywhere the sun shines and operate indefinitely.

places.name: ranawayhomenow
places.desc: Burning Man can be both an escape and an arrival. This piece captures those contrasting feelings in a single message: a change in perspective shifts "ran away" into "home now."

places.name: Heartstead
places.desc: This Installation looks like a very cozy and inviting little Heart Home, it may draw your curiosity as you see the lights shining on the inside as you peer through one of the openings, it might remind you that we all have a heart and each one is special. To me it reminds me that home is where the heart is, and you always have your heart.

places.name: Mundara
places.desc:
Mundara is a large figurative piece in a full backbend, her arm and leg outstretched creates a rainbow. 

Her backbend creates an arc between earth and sky, turning the human body into a bridge, a gateway, a horizon. The rainbow arc suggests transcendence, but also connection: the joining of opposites — masculine and feminine, human and nature, matter and spirit.

Visitors can ascend, from the ear

places.name: WiFi Jail
places.artist: Weisen Wang, Jason Wang, Nemo Wang, Yichen Dong, Ziyuan Candice Fang, Miao He, Bowei Wang
places.desc: We are a group of children (6-13 year-olds) from China, and we have made a WiFi jail. We think people are imprisoned by their phones and screens all the time. Anywhere we go, people always ask, "What's the WiFi password?" We don't look up anymore. We wanted to show what it looks if we made a blown-up version of the prison we're carrying around in our pocket. As the new generation, we're growing up

places.name: Swan Lake
places.desc: Dear comrade, come see the Swan Lake ballet on the playa, broadcast on all channels to your favorite television set. Do not worry why the ballet is being shown. Everything is all right.

places.name: BRC Aquarium Deep Research Submersible
places.desc:
PRESS RELEASE

The BRC Aquarium's Research Department is thrilled to announce the launch of our deep-water submersible research vessel, the RV MOIST-1, to advance our mission of exploring the uncharted depths and enduring mysteries of Lake Lahontan.

This ancient body of water is noted for its astonishing range of endemic fauna, many of which are new to science. The submersible will contribute

places.name: PEACE
places.artist: Omar Doctor Gago / sponsored by Playa Peace Project
places.hometown: Tulum, Mexico & San Francisco, CA, USA
places.desc:
Rising from the Black Rock Desert, the PEACE installation is a symbol of unity, connection, and collective intention. Built from steel that lights up at night, the sculpture becomes both a visual landmark and a gathering place for reflection, interaction, and shared experience.

At the beginning of the installation is the layered sculptural "P," inspired by Peace and Positivity Promotion. Together

places.name: Sphere Vision
places.desc: The two towering droids reflect the balance between creation and evolution, reminding us that as technology advances, it remains deeply connected to human intention and purpose. The LED Square serves as a portal to the universe, displaying celestial and fantastical imagery that inspires wonder, curiosity, and exploration.

places.name: Can You Read My Lips?
places.desc: A 14-foot-wide LED sign on the deep playa. Five lines of light, each reading "CAN YOU READ MY LIPS?", flicker across its face. First slow and tentative, then chaotic and overwhelming, like the fatigue of trying to keep up with many voices at once. At the peak the whole sign holds bright for one second, then resolves into a sixth line: "CAN YOU READ MY HANDS?" The piece is by a Deaf artist whose fi

places.name: Can Not Unsee
places.desc: Occupying a 15 sq ft footprint on the playa, Can Not Unsee extracts 77.9 ft³ of matter into a sparse geometric formation of minimalist poles. The installation invites participants to observe shifting perspectives, light, and spatial relationships from every angle.

places.name: Shots Fired Espresso Service - The Great Awakening
places.desc: Our coffee shop is for the Builders of Burning Man. It is a highly modified Canned Ham trailer that is now has a tilt-out counter, a sound system, solar power, a fan, and a place for our team to keep their belongings.  The trailer is 16' long in total, so it only occupies a single parking space.  There are stools for seating, and shade provided by the trailer itself.

places.name: Let There Be Light
places.artist: Omri Sasi, Liraz Uliel, Eran Klein, & Sarel Botavia Nova Heaven
places.desc: In 2026, NovaHeaven evolves into a living experience of light, form, and spiritual elevation. This year's structure is composed of 24 triangles surrounding a central hexagonal platform - 18 smaller triangles carrying the layer of remembrance, and 6 large sanctuaries inviting gathering, presence, and deep human connection. Together, these elements create an immersive field that invites us to pause,

places.name: Big Red Button
places.desc: What is this whimsical display?  Do I dare press the Big Red Button?  Wait!  This is unexpected!  And fun!  Come discover the wonders of the Big Red Button at a playa near you!

places.name: The Orb-o-Chill
places.desc:
Shelter × Intimacy × Recovery
This is a refuge for the weary Burner — a place of recovery after ecstasy. After hours of overload, light, sound, and the dense presence of other people, the desire to slow down, take shelter, feel the body, and return to inner silence arises. The Orb-o-Chill offers a state to experience: to lie down, breathe, be alone, or be beside someone. It is a soft pause within

places.name: Fuck Yer Burn Complaint Box
places.desc:
You found the Complaint Box!!! Feel free to drop a note on whatever you want to complain or comment about. There is a great chance nothing will be done, but it will be read and posted for others to complain or comment about.

If this a real emergency, hang up and dial 911. Thank you for your attention to this matter and fuck yer burn.

Sincerely,
The Department of Whining and Playa Relations

places.name: The Board Room
places.hometown: San Ramon, CA and Bend, Oregon
places.desc:
The installation is a partially enclosed booth with two facing benches and a table at its center. It appears like a small room placed in the open desert, quiet, simple, and slightly strange. On the table sits an interactive art piece created for reflection, conversation, and play.
The piece explores the moment when strangers sit across from each other and become aware of the object between them, t

places.name: The Hitchin' Post
places.desc:
The Hitchin' Post. 

Four un-assuming, Old West-style horse hitching posts have been placed around the Man for Burners to have a waypoint to meet up, hook up or engage in a Photo op. Their locations are intentional - to illustrate two playa aligned celestial moments with the Man, while also noting the seasons of the Axis Mundi Tree. Two Hitchin' Posts acknowledge the default world habit of human

places.name: Angst-in-the-Box
places.desc:
Angst-in-the-Box

Similar to a jack-in-the-box, the familiar child's toy, but different. Turning the crank will make the music, the music will stoke your expectations... but will you find the surprise you seek?

A wondrous illusion to help you meditate on anxiety and expectation... the meaning is up to you.

places.name: All Art is a Bike Rack
places.desc: All art is a bike rack on the playa. This illuminated sign is a commentary on that fact. Do burners follow directions?

places.name: The Market Commons
places.desc: A circular arrangement of colorful plastic market stools rises from the open playa, inspired by the dense social seating found in Southeast Asian night markets and street food gatherings. The installation consists of 15–25 permanently secured stools arranged in concentric circles that naturally bring participants into close proximity. In a desert where seating is rare, the piece becomes both refug

places.name: The Singularity Tree
places.desc: The Singularity Tree is a towering, cyber-organic solar punk structure pulsing with light and energy. Metallic branches stretch skyward, adorned with glowing LED vines that simulate flowing data. A central core emits a cascade of shimmering particles, creating a sense of movement and connection. Inspired by the moment where humanity and technology converge, the installation symbolizes the merging

places.name: Navagunjara Reborn: The Phoenix of Odisha
places.desc: Navagunjara Reborn: The Phoenix of Odisha is an 18-foot sculptural installation that fuses two mythical archetypes from distant traditions -- Odisha's nine-animal Navagunjara, an avatar of Vishnu in which truth is multifaceted, and the Phoenix, the universal emblem of rebirth through fire. Nine creatures rise from a single base into one vertical Axis Mundi: a dragon-headed, scale-armored body whos

places.name: Luma Lotus
places.desc: Luma Lotus is an interactive sculptural installation designed to invite rest, reflection, and meaningful connection. The piece draws inspiration from the lotus flower, known for its symbolism of growth, renewal, and emergence. The installation functions as a gentle gathering space where friends, strangers, and passersby can slow down, sit together, and reconnect, both with themselves and others, a

places.name: Dreams Never Get Old
places.hometown: South Lake Tahoe, CA, United States
places.desc: Dreams Never Get Old is a reflective camera sculpture that transforms the viewer into the subject through an oversized mirrored lens. Inspired by grief, memory, and the human desire to feel seen, the installation explores self-image and emotional reflection through a familiar object reimagined at monumental scale. The open backside of the structure creates a sheltered interior space for quiet conn

places.name: Head Maze Tickets...!
places.desc:
"Head Maze Tickets...!" is a box attached to a post of the Burning Man trash fence.  It distributes "tickets" to Head Maze.  A visitor can open the box and take a ticket.

Head Maze was at Burning Man in 2019.  There were often long lines to enter it, so there were rumors about tickets on the trash fence that let ticket holders skip the line.  There were no tickets in 2019, but there are Head Ma

places.name: Deep Playa E-bike Charging Station
places.artist: The Hash House, Wyatt McGuire & Joey Levy
places.desc: An oasis of plentiful electric power to charge your e-bike awaits you in deep playa. Some strings attached.

places.name: Light Grinder
places.desc: Light Grinder is a suspended kinetic mirrored helix flooded by an abundance of light. A continuation of Adam Frey's Grinder series, the piece builds on the spinning mirror forms of Space Grinder and Grinder Garden, shifting the focus from clustered reflection to illuminated motion. As the central helix spins, its mirrored surfaces fracture, scatter, and recombine the world around it into a twistin

places.name: Rinky Dink City
places.hometown: Penngrove, CA; Agua Dulce, CA; Los Angeles, CA; Davis, CA; Portland, OR
places.desc: Rinky Dink City is a collective celebration of the small-scale art of the playa. Arranged along a small city street, the artworks explore the essence of rinky-dinky-ness through scale, materials, and concept and empowers new artists to bring their visions to life. Rinky-dinks are characterized by approachable scale, creative use of materials, and focus on a vision over technical precision. Thus, R

places.name: Ephemeral Dust
places.hometown: San Francisco Bay Area, CA, United States
places.desc:
Ephemeral Dust is a kinetic light and dust installation that mirrors the very ritual and lifecycle of Black Rock City. Just as the city rises from the playa to form beautiful, intricate patterns before fading back into the dust, this piece continually transforms a layer of dust into an ever-changing canvas of temporary art.

The installation is composed of two elements: a central kinetic sand scul

places.name: Burning Mammal
places.desc: Inspired by Zootopia 2, this installation pokes fun at Pixar's interpretation of Burning Man by co-opting their take on the Man, infusing their IP with our own creative touches and bringing it back to the playa in physical form. A form of self-reflexive fair play, this installation will challenge participants to consider decommodification through a series of reuse.

places.name: Nippity Doo Dah
places.desc:
Hairy nipples are ubiquitous, yet they are often overlooked and under appreciated.

Invited by the fluttering hairs outside the bulbous dome, you may enter to experience this cozy nipple from the inside.

Many men, and some women, have hair circumnavigating their areola. Perhaps these hirsute areas exist to lend these furry nubbins a mysterious attraction that challenges us to explore further.

places.name: World's Highest Picnic Table
places.artist: Ditch Designed - Lisamarie Kelly & James Freeborn
places.desc:
The World's Highest Picnic Table explodes a familiar symbol of community into a monument. A table is the most fundamental thing humans create to bring people together. By scaling it sky-high, we turn this emblem of connection into a physical manifesto: the idea that community isn't passive, but something you have to actively build, climb, and claim together.

In the Deep Playa, it creates a surrea

places.name: A Second Look
places.artist: Bex and Sasha Shinn, Bat Haus Art
places.desc: All we have for sure is right now. None of us know what tomorrow, next month or three years from now will bring. Come sit, share a moment in time and take a second look.

places.name: Cats, Purrresent, and Futepurr
places.desc: Shadow cats cast onto the playa

places.name: This Blows
places.desc: A decorated windsock, a returning playa landmark for every crusty burner to enjoy. It serves as a well-known wind speed and orientation indicator for all aviators around. Black Rock Citizens wishing to watch skydivers land can use the windsock to orient themselves for the best view.

places.name: #Self-Inflatuation
places.desc:
The #Self-Inflatuation Bench is a breath of unfresh air! This art piece offers all Burners the opportunity to come sit down and self-reflect...by smelling their own farts! The shaded and serene bench is the perfect place on Playa to rest, relax, and let rip.
Influencers and commodifiers are especially welcome. After all, everyone should smell their own brand before they sell their own brand.

places.name: Chairy Go Round
places.desc: Chairy Go Round is a primitive steel beefcake of a playground ride for those seeking the nostalgic feeling of a smooth, rotating carousel of sorts. Pull-rope powered by your fellow burner, this ride will certainly scratch a long-forgotten itch for playground freedom, camaraderie, and giddy, childish giggles as the 8-seat rotating swing provides connection and joy.

places.name: The Point Being
places.hometown: Salt Lake City, UT, United States
places.desc:
A cosmic spire emerges from the playa, encircled by a courtyard and benches, creating a space for reflection and group exchange. The intricately carved etchings on the obelisk's wooden panels depict celestial and earthly motifs.

By day, the obelisk is a striking silhouette against the desert backdrop, a reminder of our unique place within time and space. As night falls, the installation glows fro

places.name: Mona Moon
places.artist: Miao He, Ricardo Solar and Bowei Wang
places.desc: Mona Moon explores emotional softness within extreme environments. The art piece is inspired in part by the ancient Chinese romantic yet tragic story of Chang'e and the Jade Bunny: Chang'e and her lover are separated when she is forced to drink an elixir of immortality and ascends to the moon. Only once a year the two lovers are able to see each other. In Chinese culture, when two lovers or family

places.name: Garden of Impermanence - AXIS MUNDI
places.desc: Choose your path and walk the Tree of Life. Lose your way — that's allowed. Dawdle at the sephiroth. Hide from the sun in the golden lantern at Beauty, where a Peacock with excellent posture has saved you a seat. Ponder your journey as the sun sets behind the Temple. Enlightenment optional. Sitting down highly encouraged. The tree isn't going anywhere. (Well. Until it is.)

places.name: Heart Beats
places.desc: Heart Beats represents one person's record collection dumped illegally in the desert and transformed into an art installation.

places.name: Petal & Piston
places.hometown: La Ventana, BCS, MX & South Lake Tahoe, CA
places.desc:
Petal and Piston includes three metal cacti sculptures, conceptually rooted from the unique desert environment of Baja California Sur.

The sculptures are primarily made from industrial-grade, repurposed materials like large towing chains and horse shoes, creating a powerful visual impact and a sense of "upcycling".

Stained-glass flower designs will bloom from the tips, adding vibrant color a

places.name: Dusty's Adventure Center
places.desc: An information booth that looks like it traveled here from a 1950s national park and got lost along the way. A glowing globe rotates on top, two wrought-iron lanterns flicker beside an incandescent INFORMATION marquee, and the side panels are covered in sun-bleached travel posters: NAVIGATE THE UNKNOWN. EXPLORE THE LAST PLAYA. Inside sits a custom-built terminal with a green CRT and clicky buttons

places.name: Are You Still There?
places.desc:
Hello?
I can't believe you're calling - it's been so long.
I am wondering if we are just borrowing bones?
Are you there?
Does your soul remain?
I miss talking with you. 
Is anyone answering these phones?
Can you hear me?
How thin is the skin between realms?
How strong is the connection?
Don't hang up. 
Who's calling?
Is the great beyond really so far away?
Is the unknown merely unanswered?
Does th

places.name: Golden Ladder
places.hometown: Santa Cruz, CA; Cologne, Germany; Katowice, Poland; Cuneo, Italy
places.desc:
The Golden Ladder - Getting people high since 6.000 BC.
Each step will take you higher, your perspective shifts, your fear goes. The EXIT is close. Turn around and see from where you came. Curious minds, standing high, you don't need to touch the stars, yet realize, every one of us is a star. Leave with freshly earned gains.

places.name: The Paradox Post
places.desc: Paradox Post is a kinetic signpost that playfully satirizes human confirmation bias. Built from scavenged materials and recycled community paint, the installation features four stacked, rotating wooden signs. Each side of the manually rotating signs displays perfectly contradictory advice, such as "Speak your truth" and "Silence is golden." The piece serves as a humorous oracle of convenient truth

places.name: Tandem
places.artist: David Posner, Jennifer Owens, and Ryan Blake
places.desc: It looks like a tandem bicycle, weeeeeeee!

places.name: Moi
places.desc: Moi is a 3ft metal divine swine sculpture.  She has learned to love herself and therefore can share that with the world, which makes her the ultimate fabulous version of all swine.

places.name: Playback
places.desc: Playback creates a bridge back into yourself, at a time where everything around you is pulling you outwards, an analog connection with your inner realm is often the most precious and human thing that you have left.

places.name: Back In 30 Minutes
places.desc: The Iron Monkeys are shifting focus from the monumental to the miniature. This year, we've forged a large steel frame of our logo and filled it entirely with a dense collage of smaller, individual art pieces. It's a reminder that even when the heavy machinery rests and the crew steps away, idle hands keep on creating. Look closely, and don't mind the sign.

places.name: Spots
places.desc:
Spots is a collection of oversized map pins appearing individually across Black Rock City, each eight feet tall, black and bold, outlined in reflective yellow tape. A six-foot flag pole rises above each pin, its label lit by solar lights at night. Every pin swivels so it can be read from any direction.

Each pin marks a specific kind of human moment: The Hugging Spot, The Giggling Spot, with more

places.name: BLACK ROCK ADVENTURES BUS STOP!
places.hometown: Los Angeles CA / Billings MT / Portland OR
places.desc: This not only looks like a bus stop, it is a BUS STOP! Playa Tours depart from the BUS STOP! Daily at 9am in our accessible adventure rig....come for a tour with us!

places.name: Soul Tree
places.desc: Soul Tree is an illuminated life size wire tree. It is a metaphor for life choices and free will, each strand being a thought or choice in ones life, the intertwined wires are self strengthening choices and actions, making branches that define a focus of our souls intention. Just as one can easily manipulate the direction of the Soul Trees wires and branches, one can manipulate their soul's trajec

places.name: I Have Dust In Curious Places
places.hometown: Another Place, Another Time, NV, United States
places.desc: It's a cheeky sign.

places.name: Conduit
places.desc: Conduit is an immersive light sculpture exploring the invisible pathways that connect people, ideas, energy, and community. A 11-foot by 13-foot steel structure incorporates laser-cut stainless steel infinity mirror panels illuminated by programmable LED lighting. During the day, layered geometric patterns create transparency and shifting views through the structure. At night, mirrored panels and

places.name: The Last Shore
places.desc:
The Last Shore is an interactive portal inspired by the disappearance of the Aral Sea, once the fourth-largest inland lake on Earth.
A freestanding frame filled with suspended reflective elements and transparent droplets creates the illusion of shimmering water suspended in space. As participants pass through the portal, a hidden soundscape evokes waves, wind, seabirds, and voices from the Aral Se

places.name: Above the Noise
places.hometown: Salt Lake City, UT, United States
places.desc: A monumental 13-foot-tall piano bench rises unexpectedly from the open playa, supporting a functioning full size grand piano high above the desert floor. Familiar in form yet impossible in scale, the installation transforms an ordinary object into something surreal, evoking wonder, vulnerability, and perspective. By day, it appears stark against the vastness of Black Rock Desert; by night, LED lig

places.name: Tengri Oasis
places.desc: Tengri Oasis is represented by a monumental reclining camel inspired by the nomadic cultures of Central Asia. Its three humps are formed by the exposed wooden frameworks of traditional yurts, transformed into transparent sculptural elements that reveal the geometry and craftsmanship of nomadic architecture. Three Altybaqan swings stand beside the camel, referencing a traditional space for gatherin

places.name: Larrys Hat
places.artist: The Office of Permits and Regulations
places.desc: "The Hat" is a site-specific installation consisting of a hat suspended above a simple illuminated platform on the Black Rock Desert. At night, lighting creates a defined square of attention within the vast openness of the playa, inviting participants to approach, gather, and linger. This well-traveled installation – appearing previously on the playa every year since Larry Harvey's death as well a

places.name: Christo at the Trash Fence, or, Curtains for Black Rock City
places.desc:
Salvaged fabric from Christo's famous 1976 landscape art, the 24.5-mile-long "Running Fence" used for curtains to beautify the trash fence.

The Running Fence was originally conceived as "Curtains for West Berlin," a project to cover the infamous Berlin Wall that separated the democratic West from authoritarian East Berlin. Black Rock City has a similar structure blocking citizens from entering fe

places.name: WG Test Walk-In 2026
places.desc:
Public Description of Installation *
Describe what your project looks like and its meaning.
Limit your description to 750 characters.
Use the third person, present tense.
Do not give commands or invite people to do things.

places.name: We Hold These Truths: E Pluribus Playa
places.desc: This mobile community recording activity moves through Black Rock City, showing up at camps, events, on the open playa, and by the ARTery. The title comes from one of the most recognizable lines in the Declaration of Independence, which marks its 250th anniversary in 2026. This project records short conversations about gathering, community, history, and shared futures in this unique moment and pla

places.name: The Only Way Out Is In
places.hometown: Dallas and Austin, TX; Joshua Tree, CA
places.desc: A tunnel of 21 nested rainbow arches. Crystal prisms hang from each arch, scattering light across the playa. The passage allows participants to reflect on their past year, its storms and its rainbows. At night, the LED-lit arches glow across the open playa. It is a meditation on transition: a reminder that every storm passes, and that it is our strife that makes the rainbow possible.

places.name: Chroma Commons at the ARTery
places.artist: Dusty Nation, Lead Artist Cameron Anne Mason
places.desc: In a temporary city in a constant state of metamorphosis, Chroma Commons creates a sense of place using ephemeral materials: Silk, color, and air. Simple yet dramatic, this moving color field activates the ARTery. Look closer and the silks reveal subtle texture and hues gradating along the color wheel. The slightest breeze creates a kinetic environment and provides changing views.

places.name: Aunisoma
places.desc: Our perception of reality is colored not only by our own emotions but through others and by the external world. How we understand something at one moment may not be the same in the next moment. We all live together in a multi-colored world that is often out of our control. This piece aims to embrace all that beautiful chaos of all these beautiful people into something to be celebrated, allowing ou

places.name: Moroccan ParTea
places.desc:
My installation art is to honor my fellow Moroccans and Moroccan hospitality; to honor their generosity and their beautiful hearts. 
A Moroccan citizen welcomes everyone with open arms and open hearts no matter their age, gender, religion, race, color - none of that matters, a mint tea is always offered from the heart and with pure love.

places.name: Photographs From Black Rock City 2000 to Present
places.desc: A wall of Burning Man photographs, exhibited at the ARTery

places.name: Fireside Circle
places.hometown: Black Rock City, NV, NV, United States
places.desc:
Welcome to The Fireside Circle! An ancient yet simple fire pit to gather around, to sit and tell stories with your new best friends that you haven't met yet, and get warm on the open playa. 

The firewood is set and ready for you to tend the fire.
 
Remember to keep the Black Rock Desert clean and beautiful. 

Leave No Trace.

places.name: String Me Along
places.hometown: The Oregon Coast, OR & Portland, OR
places.desc: Packed into a small footprint, String Me Along has the ability to have a large impact. From a distance, colors and patterns stimulate their eyes. As they get closer, they see more of the color and even more detail in the pattern. As if begging them to play, they spin String Me Along using the crystal doorknobs and watch the interplay of color, patterns, and movement. Watching the large artwork spi

places.name: Hell Station (fuel)
places.desc: Fuel + propane. 9 AM-4 PM daily; be in line by 3 PM. Distance is an estimate.

places.name: Day Care
places.desc: Bring that babe home! When the strollers park, it’s time for juicebox social, cookies and milk, and a playa naptime.

places.desc: Art HQ: registration, the art map, bike-in art tours, and where art questions go.

places.name: BMIR 94.5 FM — Burning Man Information Radio
places.desc: 94.5 FM on playa — the only broadcast that reaches the whole city with no signal and no battery but a radio. Weather, road conditions, burn times, Exodus timing, lost and found. Streams off playa via iHeartRadio. Traffic reports three times an hour during entry and Exodus. Want your event announced? Stop by 5:00 & A between 12pm and 4pm daily to record a promo. places.name: Moebius Omnibus
places.address: roams the playa · no fixed location
places.desc: An 8' round omnidirectional "flying saucer" morphed into a comfy couch with umbrella for about 12 participants to interact on.

places.name: Humblebee
places.address: roams the playa · no fixed location
places.desc: Humblebee is a polygonal adaptation of Bumblebee.  The wings will unfold on deep playa and the legs will move while driving.

places.name: the Mushroom Patch
places.address: roams the playa · no fixed location
places.desc: The Mushroom Patch is a fanciful transport for the citizens of BRC. Five giant mushrooms sprout out of a colorful plush platform which is accessible from all directions. The mushrooms provide shade during the day and glow with brilliantly changing lights at night.

places.name: Time Bandit!
places.address: roams the playa · no fixed location
places.desc: Junkyard, Steampunk Time Machine. Bending space-time & playa while bumpin' popup dance parties at the portos since 2016.

places.name: LilyPod
places.address: roams the playa · no fixed location
places.artist: LilyPad Car by Lilypad Lounge crew
places.desc: Lilypad - most comfortable way to float upon the playa

places.name: The Boob Tube
places.address: roams the playa · no fixed location
places.artist: The Boob Tube by Patrick & Evelyn Gleason
places.desc: What does every burner in the history of all burners miss the most while on the playa? Television, of course! So... Ladies and germs, freaks, hippies, yuppies, ravers, tech-bros, evil billionaires and everything in-between, the whole spectrum of burnery burnerness -- may we present to you The Boob Tube, Black Rock City's custom-built drivable TV -- bringing joy, merriment, and quality fun-casting…

places.name: Lucky Fucky Ducky
places.address: roams the playa · no fixed location
places.desc:
Once upon a splash, there lived a duck who was too big for the bathtub.
He was a trickster at heart, always stirring up
mischief, charming the flock, and dreaming of
golden horizons. Some say he's looking for trouble.
Others say he's running from bubbles.
Either way, if you see him driving by,
feathers gleaming gold, his
daring soul shining through
the stripper pole, jump on
and take a spin.

places.name: Pumablanco
places.address: roams the playa · no fixed location
places.artist: Pumablanco by Damien Otis, Ulli Bu & Puma
places.desc: Pumablanco is an all white, furry, rolling mattress during the day...transforming to a psychedelic light show at night.

places.name: Fluffy
places.address: roams the playa · no fixed location
places.desc:
Fluffy is accessible public transit masquerading as a wafting cloud to elicit and excite your dreams. A wheelchair lift and Braille rails make a mutant vehicle experience
accessible to that many more Burners. Gifting forays provide iced liquid refreshment in
the heat of the day (Deep Playa Beer Delivery) and warm gooey treats in the chill of the
night (Smores). Come Fluffy with us.

places.name: Eye Of Providence
places.address: roams the playa · no fixed location
places.artist: Eye of Providence By Trent Thomas
places.desc: The all-seeing eye symbolizes the eye of God always watching. Giving it a meta representation of week that goes on during Burning Man. Deep in the lore of the all-seeing eye is the connection to the Freemasons, giving the Eye of Providence a connection to the counterculture of society.

places.name: HEPA Filter
places.address: roams the playa · no fixed location
places.desc: The Hardly Effective Playa Anti-dust aka HEPA Filter is a whimsically ineffective device for keeping Black Rock City free of dust while providing rides for lots of burners

places.name: Little Red Rocket
places.address: roams the playa · no fixed location
places.desc:
There's something about changing an objects history or its inherent value that I find interesting. I like to invite viewers to re think the way an object is used by giving new life to the discarded, but also who I am as a person who always trys to do more with less.
The Little Red Rocket carries the same idea. Besides some of the lighting no new materials were purchased for the direct build of th…

places.name: Uuna Ahi
places.address: roams the playa · no fixed location
places.artist: Uuna Ahi mutant vehicle by camp WrongoWrongo
places.desc: A giant metal fire shooting Moai

places.name: Lola Montez Saloon
places.address: roams the playa · no fixed location
places.desc: A cozy, old west saloon serving up spirits and spirited conversation.

places.name: Dust Bunny
places.address: roams the playa · no fixed location
places.artist: Dust Bunny by Jenny Herz and Peter Millar

places.name: Chester
places.address: roams the playa · no fixed location
places.desc: A more apropriate name would be, DARK HORSE OF THE APOCALYPSE!" It's a long story.

places.name: USS Nevada
places.address: roams the playa · no fixed location
places.desc: USS Nevada is the oldest pirate ship on the Playa, bringing pirate joy and mischief all over the Playa!

places.name: Bulgarian Kuker
places.address: roams the playa · no fixed location
places.desc: Bulgarian KUKER, produced by HitterPetter Production House L.A., represents the 5000 year old Bulgarian tradition of KUKERI RITUAL DANCERS - masked people dressed up in animalistic outfits to scare away evil spirits and bring prosperity and happiness to the village.

places.name: Barbie Whorehouse
places.address: roams the playa · no fixed location
places.artist: Barbie Whorehouse by Barbie Death Village
places.desc: It is a spicy version of the well known Barbie Play House with hot pink exterior and purple accents. Riders enjoy the comfort of the first level or the second level balcony.

places.name: Snuggle Shuttle
places.address: roams the playa · no fixed location
places.artist: Snuggle Shuttle by The Schwartz brothers
places.desc: Snuggle Shuttle is a cozy rolling lounge designed to bring comfort and connection to the open playa. With soft seating, warm lighting, and an inviting atmosphere, it offers participants a place to slow down, share stories, and meet new friends while traveling through Black Rock City. More than transportation, Snuggle Shuttle is a mobile gathering space that encourages meaningful conversation, lau…

places.name: FL Man Fanboat
places.address: roams the playa · no fixed location
places.desc: The Florida Man Fanboat proudly glides across the playa rocking live music and sultry cuddle puddles to sunrise sets at the trash fence every night. A voyage supine, we bump funky beats and furry threads, ferrying you everywhere except Robot Heart.

places.name: Re-In-Karma
places.address: roams the playa · no fixed location
places.artist: Re-In-Karma by artist Sarah Plaia Davidson
places.desc:
Re-in-Karma is the stunning, double-decker beauty — now very familiar to long-time Burners. She is immediately recognizable when you see the shimmering pink wonder cruising by with a warm lie-down lower lounge and a high upper level viewing platform.
Re-in-Karma has an especially wide-open design that offers a wonderful invitation to passing pedestrian Burners. She is often seen carrying the marv…

places.name: Pillow Talk
places.address: roams the playa · no fixed location
places.desc: A rolling gold and red ornate bed experience connecting burners.

places.name: ZZYZXT
places.address: roams the playa · no fixed location
places.desc: Steam punk Inspired/Great Dane Inspired unique one of a kind vehicle.

places.name: Abu the Horsefly
places.address: roams the playa · no fixed location
places.artist: Abu the Horsefly and Abu Crew
places.desc: Abu is inspired by the 1986 animated movie by Studio Miyazaki "Nausicaa of the Valley of the Wind." This is the first insect that Princess Nausicaa defends from the angry mob. She helps Abu to find its way home. Abu teaches us that fear and mistrust are the real evils in this world, and only together we can make a difference.

places.name: Sphere Car
places.address: roams the playa · no fixed location
places.desc: This rolling dance floor is a party on 3 wheels! Lights, music and multiple observations decks. We will be rolling across the play at an unhurried pace gathering up participants as we go. Not to brag but there's even a sink with soap and running water to wash your filthy putrid hands at.

places.name: The Magic Flying Carpet
places.address: roams the playa · no fixed location
places.artist: The Magic Flying Carpet by Soren Curry and friends
places.desc: The O.G. flying carpet

places.name: Great American Phoenix
places.address: roams the playa · no fixed location
places.desc: Come join us in the nest of the Great American Phoenix! It's sure to be a bright and exciting time to soar across the playa together.

places.name: F-15 Interceptor - Black Rock Air Force
places.address: roams the playa · no fixed location
places.artist: F-15 - Black Rock Air Force by Bryan Lang
places.desc:
The Black Rock Air Force's F-15 Interceptor is a 40% scale model of the McDonnell-Douglas F-15D Eagle. On the playa since 2007, it has seen service as an Airport Follow-Me vehicle, Ranger transport, and on reconnaissance missions throughout inner and outer playa. 


It is built on an electric golf cart base and was created using fiberglass, steel, wood, foam, and high-intensity LEDs.

places.name: Flotilla
places.address: roams the playa · no fixed location
places.artist: flotilla by Willis Barnette and TMain
places.desc: Six wheeled retro 70s pontoon land yacht

places.name: Yaba Daba Do Me
places.address: roams the playa · no fixed location
places.artist: Yaba daba do me by Scooby/Chris Mcclintock
places.desc: A bitchin' two story Flintstone mobile

places.name: Butterfly love aura
places.address: roams the playa · no fixed location
places.desc: From a cocoon of love comes this butterfly to warm the hearts of everyone around. Lighting the way for all of our burner friends. We invite you to take a smaller more detailed ride on something slightly more delicate! Built by a crew from Sacramento, this piece is one of a kind!

places.name: The Jolly Trolley
places.address: roams the playa · no fixed location
places.artist: The Jolly Trolley by Steve & Shelly Lange
places.desc: We're a happy little trolley wanting to meet new friends and offer rides! We may be small out on the playa but don't let that fool you - we have BIG hearts !

places.name: Joyism
places.desc: Experience Joyism in all its forms as the yellow canopied Joyism artcar glides by.

places.name: Lady Whiskey (aka "Chooch")
places.address: roams the playa · no fixed location
places.artist: Paul Haugland, Molly Murphy, and the Chooch Crew
places.desc:
The Lady Whiskey, lovingly called “the Chooch” was originally built for Burning Man in 2011, and has evolved through the work of dedicated west coast elves.

She's a 30-foot rusty faux steam locomotive. The concept was inspired by a train graveyard in Bolivia, and originally brought to life by Paul Haugland, Molly Murphy, Philip Beber, Jessica Jensen, Brandon Lortz, Thom Orth, and many others.…

places.name: Daddy Long Wheels
places.address: roams the playa · no fixed location
places.artist: Daddy Long Wheeels by Artist Spencer Buzza
places.desc:
This mutant vehicle was built from the ground up specifically for BM.
It looks like a horseless carriage with custom 6 ft. diameter
"old wagon style" wheels. The driver and passengers ride on a big
flat comfortable piece of foam (like a queen size mattress), with a
big foam back support. The vehicle utilizes air-suspension, which can
raise and lower the vehicle like a low rider. When the suspensi…

places.name: Large Marge The Great Pumpkin
places.address: roams the playa · no fixed location
places.artist: Large Marge the Great Pumpkin by Sean Melendrez Sr
places.desc: Large Marge is a spooky carved pumpkin thats comfortable, with lots of lights Halloween decor and candy, trick or treat

places.name: Shutterbuggy
places.desc: The Shutterbuggy is a mobile photo booth modeled after a 1940s camera. You and your friends can get souvenir photos to commemorate your Burning Man experience.

places.name: Sweet Ride (was Candy Cart)
places.address: roams the playa · no fixed location
places.desc: The Candy Cart brings much needed calories to burners on the playa and beyond. Look for the gummy bears and stop by for some candy!

places.name: Passion Flower
places.address: roams the playa · no fixed location
places.desc: The Passion Flower marries kinetic, visual, and auditory elements in a multi-sensory experience of music. It is equipped with visceral and visionary artificial intelligence, 360-degree sound, and interactive lighting wrapped in blooming layers of dichroic film, Passion Flower reflects the beauty of its surroundings during the day and emits no exhaust or pollution. At night, its colorful LEDs take…
